scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Subli originated in the towns of Bauan and Alitagtag in Batangas, Philippines.
Its origin is linked to a local legend where a husband discovered a blinding light emanating from a cross-shaped tree, leading to his repentance.
This event inspired the dance as a devotional practice honoring the Holy Cross of Alitagtag.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Subli is a devotional dance honoring the Holy Cross of Alitagtag, performed during the Feast of the Mahal na Poon on May 3 and other special events like birthdays, graduations, and healing rituals.
It is not performed during Lent.
The dance fulfills a panata, or sacred negotiation, expressing religious devotion.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music of Subli is driven by the constant beating of drums and the clacking of wooden castanets (kalaste) played by men.
The rhythm is frenetic and is linked to prehispanic origins.
Listen for the drums, wooden castanets (kalaste), rondalla ensemble (theatrical versions).

The music features a continuous, driving drum rhythm punctuated by sharp wooden castanet clicks, creating a lively, ritualistic atmosphere. Women’s chants narrate the discovery of the Holy Cross in metaphorical language.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Women wear straw hats adorned with ribbons used as props for gestures such as waving, removing, and tipping in salute to the Holy Cross placed on an altar.
The dance is performed during the Feast of the Mahal na Poon on May 3 and other auspicious occasions, usually in community or church settings in Batangas.

Subli is a Philippine folk dance with prehispanic animist roots that was Christianized to honor the Holy Cross.
